content:
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days.
- Overshoots occur after sharp price spikes in the history (e.g., after 85+ values), leading to inflated forecasts that fail to correct downward.
- Mean reversion is not adequately captured: model holds onto high forecasts longer than actual price declines suggest.
- Forecast lags behind true price movements, particularly in the 10–15 day range — model reacts slower to downward trends.
- Model exhibits persistent downward bias in the latter half of the forecast (days 20–30), often underpredicting true price rebounds or stabilizations.
- When history includes a recent high, model tends to overreact with a sharp drop in forecast, then fails to recover — creating a “false dip” followed by missed rebound.
